title: Universal on New Year's Eve
titleTail: : CityWalk, the Parks, and What Sells Out
h1: Universal on New Year's Eve: the ticketed party, the parks, and what actually sells out
description: How New Year's Eve works at Universal Orlando and Universal Studios Hollywood, what the CityWalk celebration is, and why the first week of January is the better booking.
summary: Universal Orlando is the only one of the two resorts that sells a New Year's Eve product, and it is a ticketed CityWalk party rather than a park event, which makes the decision here unusually simple and unusually easy to get wrong.

typicalWindow.endsAround: the first days of January, when the holiday overlays come down

sections.heading: The short answer
body: Skip it and book the first week of January instead. New Year's Eve sits inside the busiest and most expensive fortnight of the Universal year, the parks are at capacity, and the holiday content you would be paying peak rates to see is identical to what runs in the first ten days of December at a third of the cost.

If you are already going to be there, Universal Orlando has historically sold a separately ticketed CityWalk celebration on the night itself. That is a food, drink and entertainment party across the CityWalk venues rather than a theme park event, and it is priced and booked independently of park admission.

Universal Studios Hollywood does not sell an equivalent. The park runs its normal holiday operation and closes at its normal time, and Los Angeles has a great many better places to be at midnight than a theme park car park.

sections.heading: What the CityWalk celebration actually is
body: It is a ticketed party across the CityWalk entertainment district in Orlando, typically sold in tiers that differ by which venues and which food and drink are included. It is not a park event: it does not include theme park admission, it does not give you access to rides, and buying it is not a way to be in Universal Studios Florida at midnight.

Tiers have historically ranged from a general admission ticket covering the district and its entertainment to premium packages including reserved space and open bar at specific venues. Prices are published for each cycle and move considerably between tiers, which is why we do not print a figure here — the gap between the cheapest and dearest tier is larger than the gap between two entirely different products.
It sells out, and it sells out well before the night. If it is part of your plan, buy it when it goes on sale rather than when you arrive.

sections.heading: What the parks do on the night
body: Universal Orlando's theme parks extend their operating hours on New Year's Eve and have historically run some form of countdown, but the parks are also at or near their annual attendance ceiling that night and have reached capacity in that fortnight in past cycles. Being inside the gate before the afternoon is the practical requirement rather than a tactic.

The holiday overlays are still running, which means the parade, the Grinch content and the castle projection show are all available on the night. They are the same shows they were three weeks earlier, and the queues for everything around them are not.

New Year's Day itself is marginally quieter than the night before and considerably quieter than the twenty-eighth through the thirtieth, which is the pattern most people find counterintuitive. If your dates are fixed inside that fortnight, the first days of January are the better park days.

sections.heading: The case for the first week of January instead
body: Attendance falls off a cliff at both resorts once the winter school break ends, and the drop is the sharpest of the year. Within a few days of the new year, Universal Orlando goes from its annual peak to among its quietest weeks, hotel rates fall back to their winter floor, and Express Pass returns to affordable.

The catch is that the holiday overlays come down within the first days of January and the exact date is not published far ahead, so a trip in the second week gets January prices and no seasonal content. The narrow window where both hold — low crowds and the overlays still up — is the first few days, and it is the best-value week of the whole holiday season.

The other January consideration is refurbishments. More attractions go down for maintenance in January and February than in any other window at both resorts, and Universal posts closures weeks rather than months ahead, so a January trip cannot be planned around them.

universal-orlando.verdict: The ticketed CityWalk party if you are already there and it is on sale, and the first week of January over the night itself for everybody else.
universal-orlando.note: Universal Orlando has historically sold a separately ticketed New Year's Eve celebration across CityWalk, in tiers that differ by venue access and by what food and drink is included. It does not include theme park admission and it is not a way into the parks at midnight. The parks themselves extend hours and run at or near their annual attendance ceiling that night, and have reached capacity during that fortnight in past cycles. The holiday overlays are still running and are identical to what ran in early December.

universal-hollywood.verdict: Nothing to buy. The park runs its normal holiday day and closes at its normal time.
universal-hollywood.note: Universal Studios Hollywood does not sell a New Year's Eve product. Grinchmas and the Wizarding World castle projection show run as they do throughout the season, on regular park admission, and the park closes at its usual hour. Southern California districts are on their winter break through this period, so the park is at its December peak, and the week after the new year is a markedly better booking for both crowd and price.

faqs.q: Does the CityWalk New Year's Eve ticket get me into the theme parks?
faqs.a: No, and this is the most expensive misunderstanding in this season. It is a party across the CityWalk entertainment district, sold separately from park admission, and it does not include rides or park entry. If you want to be in a theme park on the night you need a park ticket for that date as well, and you need to be inside the gate early because the parks reach capacity.

faqs.q: How much does the CityWalk celebration cost?
faqs.a: We are not printing a figure, because the tiers differ enough that a single band would mislead more than it helped, and because pricing is published per cycle rather than held from year to year. Expect a substantial gap between a general admission ticket and a premium package with reserved space and drinks included, and expect it to sell out well before the night.

faqs.q: Is New Year's Eve the busiest night of the year at Universal Orlando?
faqs.a: It sits inside the busiest fortnight, and the days between Christmas and the new year are collectively worse than any week in July. Universal Orlando parks have historically stopped admitting guests on the worst days of that stretch, which applies to people holding valid tickets who arrive late. Treat arrival time as the requirement rather than a tactic.

faqs.q: Is the first week of January a better trip?
faqs.a: Substantially, on every measure except one. Crowds collapse within days of the new year, hotel rates fall back to their winter floor, and Express Pass becomes affordable. The exception is that the holiday overlays come down in the first days of January and the exact date is not announced far ahead, so a trip in the second week gets the low prices and none of the seasonal content.

faqs.q: Does Universal Studios Hollywood do anything for New Year's Eve?
faqs.a: No ticketed product and no extended operation that we can point to across recent cycles. The park runs its normal holiday day, Grinchmas and the castle projection show included, and closes at its usual hour. Southern California is on its winter break so the park is at its December peak, which makes the night a poor combination of crowded and unremarkable.

faqs.q: When exactly do the holiday overlays finish?
faqs.a: In the first days of January across recent cycles at both resorts, with the exact date published per cycle rather than fixed. That narrow window matters: the first few days of January are the only stretch of the year with low crowds, low prices and the seasonal content still running, and a week later two of those three have gone.

freshness.sourceNote: The existence and general shape of the ticketed CityWalk celebration at Universal Orlando reflects recent cycles rather than an announcement for any future one, and no tier pricing is published here because it is set per cycle and varies widely between tiers. Capacity closures during the peak December fortnight are described from past cycles. The date on which the holiday overlays are struck is not published far ahead at either resort.
